resources.string: Messages here travel from phone to phone over Bluetooth, with no internet. Choose the name your contacts will see.
No contacts yet. When you meet someone, tap + and add each other.
Pyrsos needs the Nearby devices permission to find other phones
This phone cannot open Bluetooth channels to other phones
You must be together. Only one of you taps “Show my code”; the other taps “Scan their code”. Then the one who showed the code scans the answer that appears on the other phone.
1. Let them scan this code.\n2. Then tap below and scan the code they show you.
Now let them scan this code with “Scan their answer”. Until they do, you are not connected.
Point the camera at the code on their screen
This is not a Pyrsos code.
This code comes from a different version of Pyrsos.
That is an answer code. Tap “Show my code” first.
That answer is not for the code you are showing. Let them scan your code again.
The camera is needed to scan codes.
%s has not finished adding you. If they scanned your answer code, this clears the next time your phones are near each other with Bluetooth on. If they did not, add each other again.

On this phone (Android 10 or 11) Pyrsos does not search for other phones itself, because Android would ask for the location permission, which Pyrsos never asks for. Newer phones find this one and connect to it, so messages still arrive, sometimes a little later. Two Android 10 or 11 phones alone do not find each other.

This name goes to the other phone when you add each other, and they see it in their contact list. If you change it, people you add from now on see the new name; people who already have you keep the name they got then.
It never changes and cannot be copied. When you add someone, check that each phone shows the other\'s code.
This code is old, or the two phones show different dates. Check the date on both phones and make a new code.
You both showed your codes. Keep yours on screen: they scan it, then you scan the answer on their phone.
This person is already one of your contacts. To add them again, remove them first from the chat menu.
This code carries someone else\'s identity. Do not add this person.
Pyrsos passes messages to and from phones nearby even while it is closed. Android shows a silent notice for this. Stops by itself when the battery is low.
Pyrsos sends and receives messages only over Bluetooth. Without it nothing arrives and nothing leaves.
The messages are deleted from this phone only. Messages that have already left this phone are not deleted from other phones, and your contact keeps their copy.

The contact, its keys and the conversation are deleted from this phone only. Messages that have already left this phone are not deleted from other phones. To write to each other again you must add each other in person.
Optional. Asked every time you open Pyrsos.
Deletes all contacts, messages and your identity from this phone. Cannot be undone.

All contacts, messages and your identity are deleted from this phone, together with the key that opens them. This cannot be undone. Messages that have already left this phone are not deleted from other phones. Pyrsos closes; open it again to start over with a new identity code.
Send the app to someone next to you

Sends the app over Bluetooth to a phone next to you, with no internet: pick their phone from the list. It takes a few minutes, and they must allow installing apps from Bluetooth or their file manager.
This phone cannot send files over Bluetooth.
There are phones near you, but for a while now no connection to them has worked. This usually means your phone\'s Bluetooth has got stuck. Turn it off and on again, and Pyrsos starts again by itself.
If someone enters a wrong PIN 10 times in a row, Pyrsos deletes everything from this phone.
A second PIN. If you enter it instead of your real one, Pyrsos silently deletes everything and opens as if just installed. Useful if you are forced to open it.
Phones that connect to yours may be able to read this name, ones running Pyrsos too. A neutral name such as “Phone” says nothing about you.
Your phone has no screen lock. Without one the PIN protects much less: set a screen lock in the phone’s settings too.
This is your duress PIN, which deletes everything. Choose another PIN.
The duress PIN must be different from your real PIN.
Messages are deleted from this phone once they are older than this. They stay on the other phone. With a PIN, deleting happens when you open Pyrsos.

You have no PIN. Setting one adds a layer of security: your contacts, keys and messages are locked with the PIN and your phone\'s screen lock, so that even someone who takes your phone with special tools cannot read them. Prefer a PIN of 6 digits or more.
Messages travel from phone to phone over Bluetooth, with no internet. Keep Bluetooth on.
You add contacts only in person, with QR codes. Check together that each phone shows the other\'s identity code.
Pyrsos carries messages even while closed, but it shows no notifications for new ones: open it to see if you have any.
For extra security, set a PIN. Your messages are then locked, and someone who takes your phone cannot read them.
The key that opens your data is gone. It can no longer be opened.
The data on this phone can no longer be opened: the key that guarded it is gone, as after a reset or a restore. Start fresh to use Pyrsos again.
The old data is deleted for good and Pyrsos starts over with a new identity code. It cannot be opened anyway.
